Read and write h5ad files

Source: R/io-h5ad.R
h5ad.Rd

read_h5ad() reads an .h5ad file into an AnnData(), and write_h5ad() (also adata$write_h5ad()) writes one, following Python anndata 0.13.4 (h5ad.py). Files round trip between R and Python.

Usage

read_h5ad(
  filename,
  backed = NULL,
  as_sparse = character(),
  as_sparse_fmt = c("csr", "csc"),
  chunk_size = 6000L
)

write_h5ad(
  adata,
  filename,
  compression = NULL,
  compression_opts = NULL,
  as_dense = character(),
  convert_strings_to_categoricals = TRUE
)

Arguments

filename

Path of the .h5ad file.

backed

NULL or FALSE to read everything into memory, "r" or "r+" to keep X and raw$X on disk (read-only or read-write, see adata$file), and TRUE for "r+". as_sparse has no effect in backed mode.

as_sparse

Elements stored dense to read as sparse matrices, "X" and/or "raw/X" ("raw.X" is accepted too). An Element that is already sparse on disk is an error.

as_sparse_fmt

Sparse format of as_sparse, "csr" or "csc".

chunk_size

Number of rows (CSR) or columns (CSC) converted to sparse at a time.

adata

An AnnData().

compression

NULL, "gzip" or "lzf", the HDF5 filter applied to every dataset except scalars.

compression_opts

The gzip level from 0 to 9 (4 when NULL), which "lzf" does not accept.

as_dense

Sparse matrices to write dense, "X" and/or "raw/X" ("raw.X" is accepted too), which keeps the On-disk dtype. Dense matrices are written as they are. Unlike Python the /raw group keeps its Encoding attributes.

convert_strings_to_categoricals

Whether to convert character columns to factors before writing.

Value

read_h5ad() returns an AnnData() and write_h5ad() returns NULL invisibly.

Details

write_h5ad() replaces an existing file. With convert_strings_to_categoricals, character columns of obs, var and raw$var with fewer distinct values than rows are converted to factors in adata first, in place, as Python does. X and every layer must have at most 2 dimensions.

adata$unwriteable() reports whether the object holds a value that cannot be written, which is TRUE for a value without an encoding (a function, a Date, a partly named list) and for X or a layer with more than 2 dimensions. store_type is NULL, "h5" or "zarr" and does not change the result, because every Element that can be written to one store can be written to the other.

Files from old anndata releases are read too (also in backed mode), each Element written without encoding metadata raising anndata_old_format_warning (Python's OldFormatWarning) and writing always uses the current encodings (see read_lazy() for lazy reading).

Deviations from Python

A sparse matrix whose indices are out of range (such as 1-based indices) raises an error, where Python reads it into an invalid scipy matrix. See vignette("deviations") for the full list.

Examples

adata <- AnnData(matrix(as.numeric(1:6), nrow = 3))
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5ad")
write_h5ad(adata, path)
read_h5ad(path)$shape
#> [1] 3 2

# Backed mode keeps X on disk
backed <- read_h5ad(path, backed = "r")
backed$isbacked
#> [1] TRUE
backed$file$close()
unlink(path)
